summary: The most relevant recent papers center on pre-equilibrium and real-time QCD dynamics, rotating-QGP photon emission, physically constrained nuclear neural wave functions, and robustness-oriented physics ML. Stronger contributions either control numerical/systematic limits or encode physics constraints directly; broader ML transfer candidates remain promising but need realistic detector or event-by-event validation.
strongest_paper: Particle Production, Equilibration, and Quantum Recurrences from Classical Fields provides a clean first-principles bridge between pre-equilibrium heavy-ion dynamics and quantum-computing formulations, while the quenched-QCD topological-rate paper is the strongest controlled numerical-method contribution.

papers.title: Particle Production, Equilibration, and Quantum Recurrences from Classical Fields
papers.authors: Ivan Cuntin, Wenyang Qian, Bin Wu
papers.abstract: The paper studies particle production from classical fields, central to pre-equilibrium dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, using small-lattice lambda phi^4 simulations mapped to future quantum-computing implementations. It reports equilibration of field, occupation-number, and pressure observables before quantum recurrences appear.

papers.title: Real-time topological rate at non-zero momentum in quenched QCD
papers.authors: Claudio Bonanno, Massimo D'Elia, Roberto Dionisio, Giuseppe Gagliardi, Andrea Giorgieri, Francesco Sanfilippo, Alessandra Valentino, Giovanni Villadoro
papers.abstract: A proof-of-concept numerical study extracts a real-time topological rate at nonzero momentum in quenched lattice QCD at about 1.24 Tc using the Hansen-Lupo-Tantalo inverse-problem method and controlled continuum, smearing-width, and smoothing-radius limits.

papers.title: Photon emission from rotating plasmas: a generalized McLerran-Toimela formula and the onset of superradiance
papers.abstract: The paper derives photon emission and absorption spectra for uniformly rotating plasma in terms of current-current spectral functions and applies the result to rotating QGP photon emission, elliptic flow, and possible superradiant magnetic-field instability.

papers.title: Physics of the Electron-Ion Collider in China
papers.authors: Bo-Wen Xiao, Yuxiang Zhao, Jian Zhou
papers.abstract: An invited review of the EicC physics program, including nucleon and nuclear tomography, mass decomposition, nuclear parton structure, quantum information, and AI applications in high-energy nuclear physics.

papers.title: Variational neural-network solution of the two-body 17F proton-halo problem with a Coulomb-Whittaker tail
papers.abstract: A variational neural-network ansatz for the 17F proton-halo problem is constrained with the Coulomb-Whittaker tail and benchmarked against Numerov calculations for energies, nodes, radii, ANCs, and astrophysical S factors.

papers.title: Robust Quantum Machine Learning for Collider Event Selection under Detector Variability
papers.authors: Christopher Brown, Michael Spannowsky, Simon Williams
papers.abstract: Quantum autoencoders and quantum classifiers are compared with classical baselines for collider anomaly detection and supervised event selection under controlled feature smearing, with quantum models reportedly more stable under smearing.

papers.title: Variational Parameter Calibration with Physics-Aware Latent-Space Surrogates
papers.authors: Qiyao Zhou, Xujia Zhu, Pierre Joli, Yu Cong, Sibo Cheng
papers.abstract: An autoencoder-based differentiable surrogate for parametric dynamical systems is used for variational parameter calibration and tested on CFD benchmarks with noisy, partial, low-resolution, and masked observations.

papers.title: Spectroscopy and Dissociation of Tetraquarks in Anisotropic Plasma within the Generalized Fractional Derivatives Framework
papers.authors: H. M. Fath-Allah, M. Abu-Shady, E. M. Khokha
papers.abstract: A model study of tetraquark spectroscopy and dissociation in anisotropic plasma using a generalized fractional-derivative framework, Debye-screened extended Cornell potentials, and parametric Nikiforov-Uvarov methods.
